$comment: DarkFactory repository configuration. Documentation is built from actions with a local docs UI; legacy gh-pages is only optional preview staging.

identity.description: School project of a chess game with customizable pieces, board, and quests.

upstream.$comment: The shared pipeline. `ref` is the pin: bump it to adopt a pipeline update, and the diff shows exactly what changed.

environment.$comment: A Python application. The API reference is generated from docstrings by mkdocstrings, which properdocs still loads: it aliases mkdocs.* imports and reads mkdocs.plugins entry points.

python.$comment: TEMPORARY #239: no tests/ yet. The pinned shared CI explicitly skips pytest when no tests exist, emits a notice, and still enforces compilation, formatting, and strict docs. This is NOT behavioral coverage. Restore tests at final release gate.

release.$comment: pyproject.toml here carries only tooling configuration, so there is nothing for `python -m build` to produce and the Python distribution uses the explicit packages/ workspace. A release here is a tag and its notes, with no assets.

areas.$comment: ChessWithQuests's own domains. Declaration order is match order.

rules.description: Move generation, check and mate detection, chess rule conformance

pieces.description: Piece definitions, movement and attack vectors, custom pieces

quests.description: Quest system, objectives, progression and rewards

board.description: Board representation, custom board configurations, coordinates

docs.description: Documentation site, API reference, architecture notes

ci.description: GitHub Actions workflows, containers, runner scripts, repository automation

core.description: Controller, model wiring, application lifecycle, configuration

documentation.$comment: Sites offered by the switcher's Project axis.

license.$comment: Written from GitHub's canonical text, so it cannot drift from the wording it claims to be. NONE means deliberately not licensed for reuse, which is different from having forgotten to choose. Change it through a configuration issue.

$comment_required_checks: Written rather than defaulted: calling the pipeline as a reusable workflow prefixes every check with the caller's job name, so the unprefixed defaults would protect the branch against contexts nothing reports.
